messages:
Marcos: Heads up — after last kernel-autotune PR I’m seeing 10–15% latency regression on seq128 on a mixed A100/H100 farm. Only happens on SM102 hosts. Numbers below.

Priya: Can you paste perf profile?

Marcos: Sure, ran microbench on v2 runtime:
```
seq=64  p50=18.2ms  p95=22.1ms  tokens/sec=4500
seq=128 p50=36.5ms  p95=49.8ms  tokens/sec=3200  (old: p50=30.8ms)
KV-cache hit-rate=87%  batch_split=2  max_batch_tokens=4096
HW: sm=102 tensor_cores=true bf16=true fp8=true
```

Eli: Those p95 numbers look like batch-splitting thrash. On SM102 our kernel selection prefers the fp8 fastpath for seq>=96, but if KV cache warms differently it can split batches and trigger fallback to slower bf16 kernels.

Ben: I traced capability flags — the capability probe sets `supports_fp8=true` for SM102 iff driver reports 1.2. On some A100 driver combos it reports 1.1 and we still flip the flag due to loose compare. PR incoming.

Sanjay: Also noticing KV cache eviction spikes when mixed seq lengths present. If batch_split=2 it forces more batch boundary copies. Suggest change: prefer seq-gated batching and increase max_batch_tokens to reduce splits.

Priya: Can we add a defensive fallback: if p95(seq128) > p95(seq64)*1.3 then force bf16 fallback for seq>=96? Simple threshold until kernel pick fix.

Marcos: Good idea. Also add a quick perf test to the autotune harness: `autotune --hw=sm102 --seqlens=64,96,128 --warm_kv` and fail if p95 regress >10%.

Ben: I'll open a small patch tomorrow. putting WIP on my branch.

infra-bot: deploy request by @Ben for branch ben/kernel-sensor-fix to canary group runtime-canary-3 queued.

Eli: After patch we should re-run end-to-end with `batch_slo=8` and the live KV trace to validate no thrash.

Priya: Adding a unit test in perf-tests that injects mixed seq patterns.

Marcos: Thanks — let's aim to rollback autotune change if canary p95 > baseline. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: canary deploy started for runtime-canary-3 — will post results at 5501234609.
